Rashi on Niddah 25b:10:1.english: They bound him and he confessed - Evidently, [Shmuel] was an expert in the formation of the fetus.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:10:2.hebrew: דרב גובריה - הוא בקי, ואין כולן בקיאין:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:10:2.english: For his strength was great - He was an expert, and not everyone is an expert.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:11:1.english: A fish of the sea - There is a fish in the sea whose name is sandal [sole].

Rashi on Niddah 25b:11:2.english: Except that it was crushed - It was flattened.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:11:3.hebrew: [לשון של שור הגדול - דהיינו פניו טוחות. ואע"ג דאוקמינן לעיל פניו טוחות אין אמו טמאה, גבי סנדל ודאי אמו טמאה לידה (סנדל), דולד שעמו מוכיח עליו דולד הוא, אלא שנימוק ע"י חברו שדחקו]:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:11:3.english: [The tongue of a large bull - That is, its face is flat. And even though we established above [that if] its face is flat, its mother is not impure, regarding a sandal, its mother is certainly impure [with the impurity of] childbirth (a sandal), as the fetus that is with it proves about it that it is a fetus, only that it was crushed by its fellow who pressed against it]:

Rashi on Niddah 25b:11:4.hebrew: צריך צורת פנים אפי' מאחוריו - כלומר, אפי' אינו אלא מאחוריו, הוי ולד:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:11:4.english: Requires the shape of a face even on its back - That is to say, even if [the face] is only on its back, it is an offspring.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:12:1.english: Who slapped - He struck him on his cheek.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:14:1.hebrew: משנה זו - דקתני צריך צורת פנים, מעדותו של רבי נחוניא נשנית. הוא העיד עליה בבית המדרש, ויחידאה היא:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:14:1.english: This mishna - Which teaches that [a sandal] requires the shape of a face, was taught from the testimony of Rabbi Neḥunya. He testified about it in the study hall, and it is an individual [opinion].

Rashi on Niddah 25b:14:2.hebrew: זכה בה רב ביבי בשמעתיה - מזלו גרם לומר שמועה זו וקדמני, שגם אני שמעתיה מר' יוחנן, דמעדותו של רבי נחוניא נשנית, ולא זכיתי לאומרה:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:14:2.english: Rav Beivai merited his tradition - His fortune caused [him] to state this tradition and precede me, for I too heard it from Rabbi Yoḥanan, that it was taught from the testimony of Rabbi Neḥunya, and I did not merit to state it.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:15:1.english: And is it not [the case that] there is no sandal that does not have an offspring with it - And even without the sandal, she would be impure [with the impurity of] childbirth.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:16:1.hebrew: אי דאיתיליד נקבה בהדיה ה"נ - דלא היה צריך להזכירו, דיש לה ימי טומאה וטהרה דנקבה, שאפילו הוא זכר גמור, כי איכא נקבה בהדיה, יושבת לנקבה ימי טומאה וטהרה, ושל זכר מובלעים בתוכן:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:16:1.english: If a female was born with it, indeed so - That it would not have been necessary to mention it [the sandal], as she has the days of impurity and purity of a female; for even if it is a definite male, when there is a female with it, she observes the days of impurity and purity for a female, and those of a male are subsumed within them.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:16:2.hebrew: דאיתיליד זכר בהדיה - ומספקי' לסנדל בנקבה, ויושבת שבועיים לטומאה. אבל טהרה דנקבה לא יהבינן לה, דדילמא זכר הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:16:2.english: Where a male was born with it - And we treat the sandal as doubtfully female, and she sits [for] two weeks of impurity. But we do not give her the [days of] purity of a female, for perhaps it is a male.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:17:1.hebrew: האי נמי זכר - ולא תשב אלא לזכר, קמ"ל כו':
Rashi on Niddah 25b:17:1.english: This one is also male - And she would only observe [the period] for a male; [therefore] it teaches us, etc.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:19:1.hebrew: ד"א - אפי' ילדה עמו נקבה, צריך להזכיר ספק סנדל:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:19:1.english: Another explanation - Even if she gave birth to a female with it, it is necessary to mention the uncertainty of a sandal.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:19:2.hebrew: שאם תפיל שנים אחד לפני שקיעת החמה ואחד לאחר שקיעת החמה מונה תחלת נדה לראשון ותחלת נדה לאחרון - וה"ג לה בתוספתא. וה"פ: שאם תפיל שניהם, נקבה לפני שקיעת החמה וסנדל לאחר שקיעה, מונה לאחר שיכלו ימי טוהר לראשון תחלת נדה, וכן לאחרון. כגון, אם תראה ביום שמונים ואחד לראשון הויא תחלת נדה, דדילמא סנדל שנולד לאחר שקיעה זכר הוא, וכלו ימי טוהר שלו לסוף מ', ולא משכי בתר פ"א דנקבה. וכשתחזור ותראה בח' לראייתה ותרצה להיות סופרת יום כנגד יום, אמרינן: דלמא סנדל נקבה הוה, ומשוך ימי טוהר שלו עד פ"א לראשון, ומה שראתה ביום פ"א לראשון דם טוהר הוא, ועכשיו מה שהיא רואה ביום פ"א תחלת נדה הוא, והיינו תחלת נדה לאחרון. ובהכי הויא מקולקלת, דלא ידעינן בהך ראיה בתרייתא אי נדה היא, אי שומרת יום כנגד יום. לישנא אחרינא גרסי': שאם תלד נקבה לפני שקיעה וסנדל לאחר שקיעה, מונה תחלת לידה מן האחרון וסוף לידה מן הראשון. וה"פ: אפילו היכא דאיתיליד נקבה בהדיה הוצרך סנדל, שאם תלד נקבה לפני שקיעה והסנדל שהוא ספק זכר לאחר שקיעה, מונה תחלת לידה, דהיינו ימי טומאה, מן האחרון, דדילמא סנדל נמי נקבה היא ומנינן מיניה י"ד, שהוא ט"ו לראשון; וסוף לידה, דהיינו ימי טוהר, מנינן מן הראשון להחמיר, שאם תראה ביום פ"א, דהיינו פ' לאחרון, מטמינן לה משום נדה, דאמרי': סנדל זכר הוה, והרי ארבעים יום ששלמו ימי טוהר שלו, ודנקבה קמייתא נמי השתא כלו להו. והיינו צורך, דאי לאו סנדל הוי מנינה נמי ימי טומאה לראשון, ולא מטמאה אלא י"ד, והשתא יתבה ט"ו; ואי הוה פשיטא לן שהסנדל נקבה היא, לא הויא תחלת נדה עד פ"ב לראשון, דבתר ולד אחרון אזלינן:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:19:2.english: That if she miscarries two, one before sunset and one after sunset, she counts the beginning of niddah for the first and the beginning of niddah for the last - And this is the version taught in the Tosefta. And this is its explanation: That if she miscarries both of them, a female before sunset and a sandal after sunset, she counts, after the days of purity have concluded, the beginning of niddah according to the first [fetus], and likewise according to the last [fetus]. For example, if she sees [blood] on the eighty-first day from the first [birth], it is the beginning of niddah, for perhaps the sandal that was born after sunset is male, and its days of purity concluded at the end of forty [days], and did not extend past the eighty-one [days] of the female. And when she sees [blood] again on the eighth [day] after her [first] sighting, and wishes to count day against day [as a zavah ketanah], we say: Perhaps the sandal was female, and its days of purity extend until the eighty-first [day] from the first [birth], and that which she saw on the eighty-first day from the first [birth] was blood of purity, and now, what she sees on the eighty-first day is the beginning of niddah, and this is [the meaning of] "the beginning of niddah for the last." And in this [manner] she becomes disordered [in her reckoning], for we do not know regarding this latter sighting whether she is a niddah or a woman who guards day against day [shomeret yom keneged yom]. Another version: We learn, "That if she gives birth to a female before sunset and a sandal after sunset, she counts the beginning of childbirth from the last [fetus] and the end of childbirth from the first [fetus]." And this is its explanation: Even where a female was born with it, [the mention of] a sandal was necessary, so that if she gives birth to a female before sunset and the sandal, which is of uncertain sex [safek zachar], after sunset, she counts the beginning of childbirth, which is the days of impurity, from the last [fetus], for perhaps the sandal is also female, and we count fourteen [days of impurity] from it, which is fifteen [days] from the first [birth]; and the end of childbirth, which is the days of purity, we count from the first [fetus] to be stringent, so that if she sees [blood] on the eighty-first day, which is the eightieth [day] from the last [fetus], we declare her impure due to niddah, as we say: The sandal was male, and behold forty days have completed its days of purity, and those of the first female have also now concluded. And this is the need [to mention the sandal], for if not for the sandal, we would also count the days of impurity from the first, and she would be impure for only fourteen [days], whereas now she sits [in impurity for] fifteen [days]; and if it were clear to us that the sandal is female, it would not be the beginning of niddah until the eighty-second [day] from the first, for we follow the last offspring.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:3:2.hebrew: ומנענע באותו מקום - מלמטה למעלה, כדאמר בסמוך:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:3:2.english: And moves [it] in that place - From below to above, as [the Gemara] says nearby.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:3:3.hebrew: אם מסכסך - הקיסם, שיש דבר המעכב, היינו גיד, דאי נקבה, ליכא עיכובא:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:3:3.english: If it catches - [That is,] the sliver, in that there is something that obstructs [it], which is the male organ; for if [it were] female, there is no obstruction.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:4:1.english: From below to above - For in the fissure of the barley [grain], there is no obstruction along its length.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:5:1.hebrew: תנא אם היתה נקבה נידונת כשעורה סדוקה - לאוסופי ולפרושי אתא, דלעיל תני נידונת כשעורה, ולא תני סדוקה:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:5:1.english: It was taught: If it was female, it is judged like a cracked grain of barley - [This] comes to add and to explain, for earlier [the baraita] taught: "It is judged like a grain of barley," and did not teach: "cracked."

Rashi on Niddah 25b:5:2.hebrew: חוט - מבדיל מלמטה למעלה בין ב' הביצים, ונראה עמוק כסדק:
Rashi on Niddah 25b:5:2.english: A thread - It separates from below to above between the two testes, and appears deep like a slit.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:5:3.english: Are not discernible - They are not recognizable on account of their small size.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:6:1.english: Its two thighs - When it begins to be formed with distinct hands and feet.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:6:2.english: Woof - [It is] thicker than the warp.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:7:1.english: Do not perform an action - To treat it as an offspring until it has hair on its head.

Rashi on Niddah 25b:8:1.english: As for being concerned, she is concerned - To be stringent and observe two weeks [of impurity, as for a female birth].

Tosafot on Niddah 24b:14:1.hebrew: המפלת סנדל או שליא תשב לזכר ולנקבה - וא"ת: בשליא ליתני נמי ולנדה, דאימא הרחיקה לידתה וכבר כלו ימי טוהר, כדאיתא לקמן בפירקין (נדה דף כח.) גבי המפלת יד חתוכה — אע"ג דאמר בסמוך אין תולין השליא בולד יותר מג' ימים, להחמיר חוששין יותר מג' ימים? וי"ל, דלא דמו: דבהמפלת יד חתוכה איכא למימר דהראש או רוב הגוף כבר ילדה מקודם וכלו ימי טוהר; אבל שליא — אימא הולד בתוכה, או שלם או נימוק. ועוד י"ל, דאי הוה תני ולנדה, ה"א מביאה קרבן ואינו נאכל, דספק לידה היא — קמ"ל מביאה קרבן ונאכל. והכי נמי קאמר לקמן:
Tosafot on Niddah 24b:14:1.english: One who miscarries a sandal or an afterbirth shall sit for a male and for a female - And if you say: In [the case of] an afterbirth, let it also teach "and for a niddah", for say that her childbirth was distant and the days of purity have already ended, as is found later in our chapter (Niddah 28a) regarding one who miscarries a severed hand — even though it says nearby that we do not attribute the afterbirth to an offspring [born] more than three days [earlier], [yet] to be stringent, we [should] suspect [a delay of] more than three days? And one can say that they are not comparable: For in [the case of] one who miscarries a severed hand, it can be said that she had already given birth to the head or the majority of the body beforehand and the days of purity have ended; but [regarding] an afterbirth, say that the fetus is inside it, either intact or dissolved. And furthermore, one can say that had it taught "and for a niddah", I would have said [that] she brings an offering and it is not eaten, as it is a doubtful childbirth; [therefore,] it teaches us that she brings an offering and it is eaten. And so [the Gemara] also says later.

Tosafot on Niddah 25b:17:1.hebrew: קא משמע לן אימא שניהם הזריעו בבת אחת - לר"ת, שפירש דאין מתעברת וחוזרת ומתעברת, ואפילו נפל, אתי שפיר, וצ"ל שהזריעו בבת אחת. אבל לפרש"י, שפירש גבי ג' נשים משמשות במוך: מעוברת שמא תעשה עוברה סנדל, שולד אחרון ממעך צורה הראשונה, והא דאין אשה חוזרת ומתעברת היינו בן קיימא, (דאין) נפל חוזרת ומתעברת — לא הוה צ"ל הכא אימא שניהם הזריעו בבת אחת, והל"ל: בביאה ראשונה הזריעה היא תחלה, ובביאה שניה הזריע הוא תחלה. ומיהו י"ל, דבענין זה בב' ביאות אין חדוש למתני תשב לזכר ולנקבה, דפשיטא דפעמים הוא מזריע תחלה ופעמים היא, ולא אמר מדהאי זכר האי נמי זכר; אבל בביאה אחת, סד"א מדהאי זכר האי נמי זכר, קמ"ל: אימא שניהם הזריעו בבת אחת. ומיהו קשה: מנלן דלא אמרינן בביאה אחת מדהאי זכר האי נמי זכר? אימא לעולם אמרי', ומתני' בב' ביאות, ואשמועינן מתני' דסנדל הוי ולד אף בלא צורת פנים, ולאפוקי מעדותו של רבי נחוניא. ואע"ג דכבר אשמעינן בבכורות ובכריתות, דמייתי בסמוך, דסנדל הוא ולד, מ"מ איצטריך נמי לאשמועינן דהוי ולד לענין לידה. וי"ל דהיינו דקמשני בלשון שני. ומיהו תימה, גם לפר"ת, דלקמן (נדה דף כח.) גבי זכר וטומטום משני נמי שהזריעו שניהם בבת אחת, ותרתי למה לי? ואי אתא לאשמועינן דהוי ולד — והא כבר תנא בהדיא ברישא: טומטום או אנדרוגינוס תשב לזכר ולנקבה:
Tosafot on Niddah 25b:17:1.english: It teaches us: Say that both emitted seed at the same time - According to Rabbeinu Tam, who explained that [a woman] cannot become pregnant and become pregnant again [i.e., superfetation is impossible], even [in the case of] a non-viable fetus (nefel), it works out well, and it must say that they emitted seed at the same time. However, according to the explanation of Rashi, who explained regarding [the baraita of] "Three women engage in intercourse with an absorbent cloth (moch)" [Yevamot 12b] — "a pregnant woman, lest she make her fetus into a sandal," [meaning] that a later fetus crushes the form of the first, and that which [we say that] a woman does not become pregnant again applies [only to] a viable child (ben kayyama), [whereas with] a non-viable fetus she can become pregnant again — [if so,] it did not need to say here, "Say that both emitted seed at the same time," and it should have said: in the first act of intercourse she emitted seed first, and in the second act of intercourse he emitted seed first! However, one can say that in this manner, with two acts of intercourse, there is no novelty for [the Mishna] to teach that "she shall observe [the rules] for a male and for a female," as it is obvious that sometimes he emits seed first and sometimes she [emits seed first], and one would not say, "Since this one is male, that one is also male." But in a single act of intercourse, I would have thought to say, "Since this one is male, that one is also male"; [therefore] it teaches us: say that both emitted seed at the same time. However, it is difficult: From where do we know that we do not say, in a single act of intercourse, "Since this one is male, that one is also male"? Say that we indeed always say [so], and our Mishna is [referring to] two acts of intercourse, and the Mishna teaches us that a sandal is [considered] an offspring even without facial features, and to exclude [the ruling of] the testimony of Rabbi Neḥunya! And even though it already taught us in Bekhorot and in Keritot, which [the Gemara] cites nearby, that a sandal is an offspring, nevertheless it was also necessary to teach us that it is an offspring regarding [the impurity of] childbirth. And one can say that this is why it answers with the second version. However, it is astonishing even according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam: for below (Niddah 28a), regarding [a twin birth of] a male and a tumtum, it also answers that both of them emitted seed at the same time; and why do I need both? And if [you say] it comes to teach us that [a tumtum] is an offspring — but [the Tanna] already taught explicitly in the first clause: "A tumtum or a hermaphrodite (androginos) shall observe [the rules] for a male and for a female"!

Tosafot on Niddah 25b:2:1.hebrew: לידע אם זכר הוא - הא דאמר גויתו בכעדשה, לא שמקומו בולט, אלא שמקומו ניכר בכעדשה:
Tosafot on Niddah 25b:2:1.english: To know if it is male - That which [the baraita] says, "its body [i.e., the male organ] is like a lentil" — [it does] not [mean] that its site protrudes, but rather that its site is discernible like a lentil.
